about: The phone remote, seen from where you sit: the TV ahead, centred, and below it the phone in your hand, tilted away, its touches shown on its screen. The film is the phone film (tools/scenes.py draws it; without it the remote's film stands in, with the beats it has). Each beat plays one part of the film; each gesture is where a touch lands on the phone's screen (in % of its picture), a moment before the TV answered that press (the film's own timeline, site/data/FILM.json). A beat whose part the film doesn't have is left out.

beats.label: Swipe
beats.says: Swipe on the phone, and the TV moves along the dock.

beats.label: Tap
beats.says: Tap the middle of the touchpad, and the TV opens what's chosen.

beats.label: Back
beats.says: Back on the phone closes it again.

beats.label: Volume
beats.says: The volume, from the phone. The TV shows it as it changes.

beats.label: Home
beats.says: Home on the phone: the weather closes and the desktop is back.

beats.label: Glass
beats.says: Glass on the phone opens the assistant on the TV, listening.
